Fourth, core-valence decoupling: the core-valence mutual information falls to $\approx 4×10^{-3}$ by $Z = 4$, decays monotonically through $Z = 6$, and reaches the $\approx 10^{-15}$ floating-point noise floor for $Z \geq 7$ — an exact core-closure property of this basis (the $1s$ occupation is exactly $2$), so it constrains the basis rather than justifying the composed fiber bundle factorization used in the GeoVac molecular framework. In the composed molecular architecture, per-block entanglement is $R$-independent by construction, with a bond/core entropy ratio of about $40×$ (block Hamiltonians without the Phillips–Kleinman term; about $57×$ with it). These results establish that the angular momentum eigenbasis isolates correlation and entanglement in the two-body $V_{ee}$, and that the Gaunt sparsity of the GeoVac qubit Hamiltonians — whose Pauli count is exactly linear in the qubit count at fixed basis — is a direct consequence of this basis choice. This is Paper 26 in the GeoVac series.

title: Entropy as a Projection Artifact: One-Body Operators are Entanglement-Inert on Sparse Lattices
abstract: We characterize the operator-theoretic origin of entanglement entropy in the GeoVac Coulomb lattice, a finite spectral graph realization of the hydrogenic angular momentum eigenbasis on $S^{3}$. Five results are presented. First, the von Neumann entropy of any single-particle reduced density matrix derived from a non-degenerate ground state of a purely one-body fermionic Hamiltonian on a finite lattice is identically zero; numerically, we confirm $S_{\mathrm{kin}}/S_{\mathrm{full}} \sim 10^{-14}$ at $n_{\max}=2,3$ on a He model whose one-body operator is deliberately non-diagonal in the angular momentum eigenbasis (for helium's physical, diagonal one-body operator the zero is exact). All ground-state entanglement is generated by the two-body interaction $V_{ee}$, with the non-degeneracy qualifier essential: open-shell and dissociated-bond states escape the floor. Second, the holographic area-law scaling $S_n = k\log A_n$ with $A_n\propto n^{4}$, asserted on one-particle grounds in earlier framework papers, is recovered as a pair-counting statement: $A_n=g_n^{2}$, where $g_n=2n^{2}$ is the shell degeneracy. The factor of four is the two-body signature. Third, in the Coulomb lattice the cusp concentrates as a single ``hot node'' on the $(1s,1s)$ pair-state of the $V_{ee}$ graph; since entropy is generated exclusively by $V_{ee}$, this is also the locus of entanglement mass: an edge-resolved decomposition puts $58.5%$ of helium's correlation entropy on the single hottest $V_{ee}$ edge, though not all of it: removing the largest off-vertex edge in the ground state's symmetry sector, half as strong, raises it by $14%$. Fourth, a previously claimed rigidity statement — that the ground-state entropy of any two-fermion closed-shell state on the Bargmann–Segal harmonic oscillator lattice interacting via any central two-body potential is identically zero, by Moshinsky–Talmi total-quanta conservation — is retracted here (\S(ref)): the Moshinsky–Talmi bracket conserves total quanta, the potential matrix element does not, and the published zero was a code artifact. The corrected entropy is small but nonzero and grows with basis size. Fifth, Coulomb-lattice block entropy obeys a universal scaling $S_B = A (\tilde{w}_B/\delta_B)^{\gamma}$, where $\tilde{w}_B$ is the dimensionless $V_{ee}$ mass off-diagonal in the one-body eigenbasis and $\delta_B$ the dimensionless first $H_1$ gap; the local exponent extrapolates to $\gamma_{\infty} \approx 1.96$–$1.97$ in the $n_{\max}\to\infty$ limit in the $Z:15\to30$ window (extrapolated from $n_{\max}=2$–$7$ on helium-like ions' physical Hamiltonian; fixed-$n_{\max}$ local slopes reach $1.91$ by $Z=100$; an earlier $1.93$–$1.96$ was measured on a hop-augmented model one-body operator), slightly below the non-degenerate second-order Rayleigh–Schrödinger value of $2$. The gap is the logarithm in the von Neumann entropy: $S\approx\varepsilon\ln(1/\varepsilon)$ with a correlation weight $\varepsilon$ that scales at the second-order rate, so at fixed $n_{\max}$ the local exponent returns slowly to $2$ as $Z\to\infty$. Entropy is slotted into the exchange-constant taxonomy as a projection-class observable: zero on the combinatorial graph (non-degenerate case), finite only after the metric embedding of $1/r_{12}$.

title: GeoVac as a Two-Layer Framework: Projection Taxonomy and the Empirical Matches Catalog
abstract: The GeoVac framework decomposes into two structurally separate layers. Layer 1 is a bare combinatorial graph: quantum-number labels $(n,\ell,m,\ldots)$, rational matrix entries, algebraic eigenvalues, no physics. Layer 2 is a finite family of named projections from the bare graph onto physical settings. Every physical variable, every dimensional unit, and every transcendental constant that appears in any GeoVac calculation enters through exactly one projection (apart from external inputs—literature values and applied field strengths—and textbook-assembly rows of the catalogue—vacuum polarization, self-energy, tabulated Bethe logarithms—which enter through no GeoVac projection), and is fully traceable to it. We catalogue twenty-eight projection mechanisms and tag each one along three independent axes: (a) which physical variables it introduces (charge $Z$, coupling $α$, energy scale $\hbar\omega$, internuclear distance $R$, gauge coupling $\beta$, cutoff $\Lambda$, $\ldots$); (b) which physical dimension or unit it attaches to graph data (energy, length, dimensionless, solid angle); and (c) its transcendental signature in the sense of Paper 18 (rational, $π^{2k}$, half-integer Hurwitz, odd $ζ$, Dirichlet $L$, $\ldots$). The projection axis is a structural sibling of Paper 18's transcendental axis: each transcendental tier corresponds to a specific projection type, and reading the dictionary in either direction recovers the other. We then assemble the empirical matches catalogue: a tagged table of GeoVac quantities compared with standard physics values, with residuals ranging from machine-exact to non-converged. Each row is annotated by projection(s), variable(s), dimension, transcendental class, and match precision. Reading the catalogue suggests a structural Observation: \begin{observation}[Layer-2-presence bound.] The residual error of a catalogue row is bounded above by the larger of (i) the framework's basis-quality residual at zero Layer-2 inputs, and (ii) the largest single Layer-2 input consumed by the chain. Equivalently: $|\epsilon(observable)| \leq \max\bigl(\epsilon_basis(framework), \max_i |L_2^{(i)}|\bigr)$. The genuine axis ordering catalogue precision is observable-class (zero-, one-, multi-Layer-2-input) crossed with the framework's basis-quality limit; chained projection depth is a downstream proxy that fails in both directions. \end{observation} The zero-input rows are consistent with it; the one-input class has no clean member, and one row, the corrected D 1S HFS, violates it (\S(ref)). This replaces an earlier naive form that scaled residual linearly with chain depth; the May 2026 synthesis pass falsified the depth form on the catalogue itself (depth-3 chains exist at residual $0$ and at $-456$ ppm; a depth-4 chain exists at $+2$ ppm). The H 1S polarizability example (depth-3 chain, residual $0$) is consistent with the zero-Layer-2-input class for rational-analytic-answer observables. The hydrogen Lamb shift is outside the catalogue's projection chains: it is a textbook one-loop assembly with tabulated Bethe logarithms (Paper 36). Apart from Remarks (ref) and (ref), which report new measurements with dedicated backing tests, this paper introduces no new computation. It is a structural consolidation of the framework's self-presentation: language for discussing where physics enters, what carries dimensions, and which transcendentals are forced by which projection.

title: Time as Projection: The Klein-Gordon Spectrum on S^3 × ℝ and the Algebraic / Observation Split
abstract: The bare relativistic Klein-Gordon spectrum on $S^3 × ℝ$ is $π$-free in the algebraic-extension ring $\mathbb{Q}[\sqrt{d_1}, \sqrt{d_2}, \ldots]$ with $d_i$ positive square-free integers, for every rational mass-squared parameter. We verify this symbolically for $n \in [1, 50]$ across the panel $m^2 \in \{0, 1, 1/4, 2\}$ (200 cases, zero transcendentals). Mass is therefore a parameter projection that preserves the bare-graph algebraic ring; it does not introduce $π$. $π$ enters the spectrum at exactly one step: temporal compactification. On $S^3 × S^1_\beta$ the temporal direction acquires Matsubara modes $\omega^t_k = 2π k / \beta$, and the first $π$-bearing eigenvalue is the $(n{=}0, k{=}1)$ mode with $\omega^2 = 4π^2$. We exhibit the before/after explicitly: every $(n, 0)$ eigenvalue is $π$-free; every $(n, k {\neq} 0)$ eigenvalue contains $2π/\beta$. The conformally coupled massless scalar Casimir energy on unit $S^3$ (spatial only, no temporal compactification) evaluates to the exact rational $E_Cas = 1/240$, with no transcendental content at any step of the $ζ$-regularized derivation. The Stefan-Boltzmann constant $π^2/90$ appears in the high-temperature expansion of the free-energy density on $S^3 × S^1_\beta$ only via the Matsubara sum, exactly through the mechanism of the spectral $π$-injection. Paper 34's projection dictionary splits the implicit ``scalar parameter projection'' into (i) a rest-mass projection (introduces $m$, dimension mass, transcendental signature trivial, ring-preserving for $m^2 \in \mathbb{Q}$) and (ii) an observation / temporal-window projection (introduces $\beta$, dimension time, transcendental signature $2π \cdot \mathbb{Q}$ per Matsubara mode; Stefan-Boltzmann $π^2/90$ in the high-$T$ limit). These are categorically distinct; lumping them as a single ``parameter row'' under-resolves the transcendental axis of the dictionary. The structural reading is sharper than Paper 34's layer description: a GeoVac observable contains $π$ if and only if its evaluation includes a continuous integration over a temporal or spectral parameter that has been promoted from the discrete graph spectrum. The discrete graph itself is $π$-free; the projection that integrates is where $π$ appears. Existing GeoVac observables (Pauli counts, magic numbers, hydrogenic eigenvalues, Bargmann–Segal lattice, the graph QED ground-state self-energy) are confirmatory; the canonical $π$-bearing observables (vacuum-polarization $\Pi = 1/(48π^2)$ and $\beta$-function $2α^2/(3π)$, the standard flat-space values, and Stefan-Boltzmann) are all evaluated through continuous integrations of the temporal kind. Beyond the verification sprints $\mathrm{KG}-1$, $\mathrm{KG}-2$, $\mathrm{KG}-3$ and the closed forms reported in Sections (ref) and (ref) (among them the $S^5$ conformal $-31/60480$ and the Bargmann–Segal harmonic-oscillator $-17/3840$, both computed here), this paper introduces no new computation. Its contribution is the structural observation that time, not mass, is the projection axis along which $π$ enters the framework, and that the observer's finite-time measurement window, read as a periodic Euclidean circle (an identification the paper adopts rather than derives; Proposition (ref)), is the formal mechanism.

title: The Leading One-Loop Hydrogen Lamb Shift: Assembly, a Convention Erratum, and Coulomb-Sturmian Bethe Logarithms
abstract: We assemble the hydrogen $2S_{1/2}$–$2P_{1/2}$ Lamb shift at leading one-loop order, $α(Zα)^4$, from the standard expressions reviewed by Eides, Grotch and Shelyuto, with the electron mass in place of the reduced mass and the Bethe logarithms tabulated by Drake and Swainson. The result is 1052.19 MHz, $5.65$ MHz ($0.534%$) below the Lundeen–Pipkin measurement, 1057.845(9) MHz, and $5.64$ MHz below the 2019 measurement of Bezginov et al., 1057.8298(32) MHz. This is textbook arithmetic, and the residual is not a measure of missing multi-loop physics: the self-energy part of the one-loop $α(Zα)^5$ term alone, with coefficient $A_{50} = 4π(139/128 - \tfrac12\ln 2) \approx 9.29$, adds about $+6.9$ MHz, more than the residual. Adding the review's other tabulated terms down to the kHz level gives $1057.824$ MHz, $0.020$ MHz below Lundeen–Pipkin and $0.005$ MHz below Bezginov et al. The paper records three things. First, an erratum: an earlier assembly used the self-energy constant $38/45$ in place of $10/9$. The difference is exactly the Uehling coefficient $4/15$, which had been subtracted inside the self-energy while the Uehling shift was also added separately; restoring $10/9$ moves the Lamb shift by $+27.13$ MHz. Second, Bethe logarithms computed from scratch in a Coulomb-Sturmian pseudostate basis at exponent $Z/n$: $\ln k_0(2P)$ and $\ln k_0(3D)$ reproduce the tabulated values to $2.4%$ and $0.07%$ with 40 basis functions ($2P$: $1.24%$ with 55), while the $2S$ acceleration-form value is not converged ($-0.92%$ at 40 functions is a crossing; $+2.98%$ at 50). Third, a negative result: a model two-loop self-energy sum on the Dirac spectrum of the three-sphere grows without bound with its cutoff and yields no finite two-loop coefficient without renormalization counterterms, which it does not contain. Evaluating hydrogen Bethe logarithms through the dynamical symmetry of the Coulomb problem is prior art (Lieber, 1968; Huff, 1969).

title: GeoVac: A Field Guide From a Packing Puzzle to an Atlas of the Forced/Free Boundary
abstract: The Geometric Vacuum (GeoVac) framework began as a packing puzzle that produced something resembling the periodic table. Over the course of the investigation, it acquired a precise structural identity: a discrete spectral triple that is an instance of the Marcolli–van Suijlekom 2014 graph-network construction at the data level and extends it via a forced-graph claim and a master Mellin engine, whose census of $S³$ spectral transcendentals sits in cyclotomic mixed-Tate periods at level $\le 4$, and which separates — through theorems and named readings, not preference — what the underlying geometry forces from what empirical measurement supplies. This field guide is the project's identity statement. It tells the arc from origin to current frontier without recapitulating the technical machinery, and points each kind of reader toward the right entry into the corpus. As the project's grand synthesis it now sits atop a complete layer of six audience-targeted group syntheses—one per branch (Groups 1–6), each digesting its branch in a few pages—and composes them into a single front-to-back reading that routes each reader to the right branch digest. Re-centred October 2026: the spectral triple is one chapter of the map, not its spine. The spine is an accounting. Compactness forces discreteness (a mechanism that is not ours, and whose converse is false), so the compact skeleton is rational and bit-exact; every axis released toward the continuum — by geometry, by an observer, or by calibration — carries an identifiable number class as its price; and the atlas of those prices (\S(ref)) is the deliverable. The one-sentence reading: GeoVac is the price list of leaving a compact world:\ its label lattice is the rational skeleton that compactness forces, each released axis carries a named number class as its price, and the atlas of those prices separates what geometry forces from what measurement supplies.

title: The operator-algebra arc of the GeoVac framework: a reading guide for spectral triples, state-space Gromov–Hausdorff convergence, and the Lorentzian question
abstract: We provide a unified reading of the fourteen papers that make up the operator-algebra arc of the GeoVac framework (Papers 29, 32, 38, 39, 40, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49, 50). The arc constructs an explicit almost-commutative spectral triple $(\AGV, \HGV, \DGV)$ on the Fock-projected unit three-sphere with a Camporesi–Higuchi spinor Dirac operator, places it in the Marcolli–van Suijlekom gauge-network lineage, and establishes four load-bearing results. First, the underlying truncated graphs are Ramanujan at small sizes — a finite-size graph-RH Observation (two of four families cross the irregular Ramanujan bound at modest sizes, through real eigenvalues, Paper 29 \S7), with integer-algebraic Ihara zeros (Paper 29). Second, \gvc{wh1-p38-gh-convergence}{the Connes–van Suijlekom truncations $\Tcal_{n_max}$ converge to the continuum spectral triple $\Tcal_{S³}$ in the van Suijlekom state-space Gromov–Hausdorff sense — for the commutative ($S^3$) factor on the true Camporesi–Higuchi window; convergence of the almost-commutative extension is [OPEN]} — \gvc{p38-rate-constant}{with the Fejér-kernel bound $d_{\mathrm{GH}}(\Tcal_{n_max}, \Tcal_{S³}) \le \gamma_{n_max}$, $\gamma_{n_max} \sim (4/π)\logn_max/n_max$, and a measured $O(1/n_max)$ under a tapered amplitude (Paper 38, main theorem; $4/π$ in the dual-Coxeter normalisation of the $SU(2)$ metric, $2/π$ on the unit $S^3$)}. Third, Paper 40 extends the convergence to compact connected semisimple Lie groups (conditionally for general $G$); whether the Fejér-moment constant is the same for every simple group is [OPEN], since its rank-2 extractions used a normalisation that does not reproduce the $SU(2)$ anchor. Fourth, the natural route to a Lorentzian convergence theorem on truncated $SU(2)×U(1)_{t}$ Krein spectral triples — compressing to the Krein-positive subspace — is closed by a degeneracy theorem (Paper 45): the compression annihilates the spatial Dirac and the restricted Lipschitz seminorm vanishes identically. An earlier convergence claim through this device, together with the strong-form and bridge extensions built on it (Papers 46, 48, 49), is withdrawn; the Lorentzian analog of the convergence question Connes and van Suijlekom [ref] deferred to ``elsewhere'' (answered on the Riemannian side for scalar compact groups by Gaudillot-Estrada and van Suijlekom, and for the spinor triple's commutative factor by Paper 38) remains open, now with a sharpened specification. Paper 47's de-compactification limit $T \to \infty$ survives at the norm-resolvent / spectral level. A master-theorem sketch (\S(ref)) subsumes Papers 38, 39, and 40 as special cases: \gvc{p40-general-g-conditional}{for arbitrary $k \ge 1$ and compact connected simple Lie groups $G_{1}, \ldots, G_{k}$, the k-fold tensor product converges (state-space GH) with per-factor Fejér-moment bounds, leading constant open beyond $SU(2)$ in Paper 40 (proved only for $SU(2)$ and $SU(2)×SU(2)$, on the lifted-state route with leading constant $1$; the general-$G$ $k = 1$ case is conditional on the per-group spin-window decomposition; the joint Lipschitz constant $C_3^{(k)} = 1$, by compression, belongs to the abandoned approximation-pair route)}. \gvc{m1-gh-rate-reading}{The Fejér-moment constant $4/π$ (Paper 38) is read — convention-dependently (dual-Coxeter normalisation) and as a reading, not a derivation — as the $M_{1}$ ($k = 0$ volume-slot) signature of the master Mellin engine, whose case-exhaustion (Paper 32 \S VIII) is [CONDITIONAL]}; the reading concerns the kernel's constant, not the GH rate; the $1/π^{2}$ of the Lorentzian HS-orthogonality (Paper 42 \S 11.7) is not shown to be the same signature — it is the square of the posited normalisation $\beta = 2π/\kappa_g$. Further papers (48, 49, 50, 53) extend the arc; Papers 48–50 are recorded in \S(ref)–\S(ref), and Paper 53 is summarized at the end of this abstract (Paper 52 is archived); metric-level claims among them descoped by Paper 45's degeneracy theorem are reported here in corrected form. title: The Natural Geometry Hierarchy: A Synthesis of the GeoVac Quantum-Chemistry Arc
abstract: The Geometric Vacuum (GeoVac) framework discretizes non-relativistic electronic structure on natural geometries: for each separable quantum system there is a coordinate system in which the Coulomb singularities become boundary conditions and the Laplace–Beltrami operator's quantum-number structure (labels, degeneracies, selection rules) is carried exactly by a sparse lattice whose nodes are those labels. This synthesis assembles the framework's quantum-chemistry arc—the thirteen Group 2 papers spanning one-electron atoms, the two-center one-electron ion, the two-electron atom, the two-center two-electron molecule, the core–valence and polyatomic extensions, the genuine two-center tensor census, the transcendence frontier at the third center, the isoenergetic Sturmian secular equation, and an equal-size basis comparison on water—into a single coherent narrative organized by the natural geometry hierarchy. The hierarchy is a grid indexed by the number of nuclear centers and the number of electrons: $S^3$ (Fock) for atoms [ref], the prolate spheroid for $\mathrm{H}_2^+$ and $\mathrm{H}_2$ [ref], hyperspherical coordinates for He [ref], molecule-frame hyperspherical coordinates as the structural $N$-electron generalization [ref], and composed fiber bundles for core–valence and polyatomic systems [ref]. Three threads run through the arc. First, an algebraic-first program: the angular content is computed exactly from Gaunt coefficients and Wigner $3j$ symbols at every one-centre level and in each Level-5 fibre (at the two-centre prolate level only the axial $m$ label is exact, Paper 0), the prolate-spheroidal electron–electron repulsion is replaced by an algebraic Neumann expansion [ref], the radial solvers reduce to three-term Laguerre recurrences, and the split-region Legendre nuclear coupling terminates exactly via the $3j$ triangle inequality [ref]; what currently survives as quadrature ($Z_{\mathrm{eff}}$ screening, the adiabatic potential curves, the hyperradial coupling) is named explicitly, and finding algebraic replacements is an ongoing goal rather than a deficiency. Second, two structural negative results delimit the design space: in the single-$n$ $D$-matrix approximation to a single-center molecular Sturmian basis with a shared momentum scale, the one-electron Hamiltonian and overlap obey the two-term identity $H_{ij} = -\tfrac12 p_0^2 S_{ij} + (1-\beta_j)V_{ij}$ and share a single orthogonal $SO(4)$ Wigner-$D$ congruence, so the generalized eigenvalues are independent of the internuclear distance and cannot bind unless the Sturmian scale $\beta_k(R)$ itself becomes $R$-dependent [ref]. (Paper 8's own scope remark is explicit that this delimits that approximation and is not a no-go for Sturmian molecular binding: the genuine cross-$n$ Coulomb–Sturmian overlap breaks the shared congruence and supplies the $R$-dependence algebraically—see the Paper 60 entry below, where the method binds.) And a graph built by concatenating atom-centered lattices has an $R$-independent intra-atomic kinetic energy, producing a monotonically attractive potential-energy surface with no equilibrium [ref]. A later genuine two-center census sharpens where the sparsity lives: evaluated over orbital products that span two nuclei the Gaunt $l$-selection rule fails and only the axial $m$-rule survives, so the angular sparsity is an atomic-sector property—the abelian residue of the molecular point group [ref]. Third, honest accuracy ceilings: the framework reaches machine precision for $\mathrm{H}_2^+$, \gvc{he-bracket}{$0.022%$ (properly variational, raw $l_{\max}=7$) and $0.020%$ with the Schwartz cusp tail at $l_{\max}=4$, still above exact, for He}, $99.97%$ of $D_e$ ($0.053$ mHa) for $\mathrm{H}_2$ via an explicit-$r_{12}$ extension of the prolate spheroidal engine with exact algebraic integrals ($99.81%$ / $0.32$ mHa via re-conditioned CI at a larger truncation and the variational optimum $α = 1.40$)—and $96.0%$ (on an unconverged inner hyperradial wall) in the molecule-frame hyperspherical treatment—two routes to the same system, not a matched pair, and $\mathrm{H}_2$'s natural geometry is the prolate spheroid—and—in the composed architecture, whose accuracy bottleneck is the Phillips–Kleinman pseudopotential—$5.3%$, $11.7%$, and $19.4%$ equilibrium-bond-length error for LiH, $\mathrm{BeH}_2$, and $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ respectively. The classical-solver investigation is complete: its accuracy ceilings are characterized, and the framework is positioned as a zero-parameter, structurally sparse research instrument—a computationally principled alternative whose primary downstream value (qubit-Hamiltonian sparsity for quantum simulation) lives in the quantum-computing arc—not as a replacement for production quantum chemistry. The discrete label lattice and the continuous Laplace–Beltrami operator are dual descriptions of the same quantum-number structure, linked by an exact Peter–Weyl label identification (the lattice's labels are those of the $S^3$ harmonics, on which the operator acts as the diagonal $SO(4)$ Casimir), with Fock's proven conformal projection linking the operator to the Schrödinger equation (\gvc{graph-s3-wall}{the lattice's graph Laplacian is not one of the two: it does not converge to $\Delta_{S^3}$, Paper 7}); the interpretive question of which is more fundamental is left open.

title: Foundations of the Geometric Vacuum Framework: A Synthesis of the Spectral Graph Theory Arc
abstract: The Geometric Vacuum (GeoVac) framework is a discretization scheme for non-relativistic quantum mechanics on natural geometries, built on a packed lattice of quantum-number labels. For hydrogen the lattice's nodes are exactly the labels of the unit-$S^3$ harmonics, on which (minus) the continuous Laplace–Beltrami operator acts as the diagonal $SO(4)$ Casimir at every cutoff; \gvc{graph-s3-wall}{the lattice's edge Laplacian does not replace or converge to that operator (it splits into $n_{\max}$ disconnected $l$-blocks)}. This synthesis paper assembles the framework's foundational arc—the packing construction, the discrete graph and its dynamics, the conformal equivalence with the unit $S^3$, the exchange constant taxonomy, the angular sparsity theorem, the Bargmann–Segal lattice, and the universal/Coulomb partition, together with the reconvergence node where these threads cohere (the tensor-product triple's two-body interaction and where it stops, the period census, the Tannakian substrate and cosmic-Galois comparison homomorphism, and the forced/free seam)—into a single coherent narrative. The arc has a dependency structure worth naming: a single taproot (the packing construction, made physical by the Fock $S^3$ projection) fans out into the framework's machinery, then reconverges at the periods, Tannakian, and forced/free nodes, where the scattered structural findings cohere into one statement about what the framework forces and what it consumes. Four headline structural results frame the program: [SYMBOLIC PROOF] (a) the conformal chain from the continuum operator onward — the unit-$S^3$ Laplace–Beltrami operator, its integer spectrum ([PRIOR ART], checked for $n \le 4$), and the energy-shell projection, under which the hydrogen bound-state Hamiltonian is $H = -\tfrac{Z^2}{2}(1-\Delta_{S^3})^{-1}$ — audited by a suite of 18 symbolic checks, with the non-definitional energy step (the $S^3$ Coulomb kernel's eigenvalue $2π^2/n$ forcing $p_0 = Z/n$) carried by the exact kernel-eigenvalue test of Paper 7 ($n \le 4$; general $n$ is Fock's); [WALL] the discrete Fock \gvc{graph-s3-wall}{graph's edge Laplacian does not converge to that operator (it splits into $n_{\max}$ disconnected $l$-blocks with an $n_{\max}$-dimensional kernel)}; what is exact is its label set, on which the operator is the diagonal $SO(4)$ Casimir (the 18 checks do not touch the graph-side step) (ten of the eighteen limiting-case, definitional or non-discriminating rather than logically independent, Paper 7); [PRIOR ART mechanism; the explicit densities are new] (b) the angular sparsity of two-body matrix elements depends only on $l_{\max}$ and is bit-identical across five distinct central potentials, qualifying as a potential-independent theorem about spherical-fermion bases; [PANEL-VERIFIED] (c) the three-dimensional isotropic harmonic oscillator admits a discrete graph encoding on the Hardy space $H^2(S^5)$ that is bit-exactly $π$-free in exact rational arithmetic at every finite cutoff; [OBSERVATION] (d) the framework's results split cleanly along an A/D partition—an algebra-only universal sector that transfers free across central potentials, and a Dirac-operator-specific sector containing the spectrum, the projection, and the candidate fine-structure-constant combination of Paper 2 [ref]. [OBSERVATION] A structural reading we make explicit in this synthesis is that the framework's substrate-level scale-freedom—the packing diameter $d_{0}$ cancelling out of every spectral quantity, and physical scales entering only through the Fock-projection focal length $p_{0}$—is the geometric expression of the same principle that conformal field theory embodies at the physics level (cf. the F-theorem of [ref]). GeoVac provides a scale-free mathematical substrate; CFT is a scale-free physics theory living on such a substrate. This is not a claim that GeoVac is a CFT; it is a structural reflection consistent with (not evidenced by) Paper 50's closed-form re-derivation of the continuum CFT-on-sphere free energies, in which the truncation never enters (operator-algebra arc, outside the foundations scope of this synthesis). We present GeoVac as a discretization framework that exploits natural geometry, not as a new foundation for quantum mechanics: the discrete label lattice and the continuous Laplace–Beltrami operator are dual descriptions linked by an exact Peter–Weyl label identification, with Fock's conformal projection linking the operator to the Schrödinger equation (the bound-state Hamiltonian is $H = -\tfrac{Z^2}{2}(1-\Delta_{S^3})^{-1}$), and the interpretive question of which description is more fundamental is left open. The framework's concrete computational advantages—$O(V)$ sparsity, angular momentum selection rules baked into the basis, bit-exactly rational squared matrix elements on the Bargmann–Segal lattice, and the universal sparsity bound—are independent of that interpretive question. (The integer spectrum $n^2 - 1$ is a property of the continuum operator, not of the graph, whose closed-form spectrum is bounded in $[0, 8]$.)

title: Structural Sparsity for Quantum Simulation: A Synthesis of the GeoVac Quantum-Computing Arc
abstract: The Geometric Vacuum (GeoVac) framework discretizes electronic structure on natural geometries, producing sparse Hamiltonians in natural-geometry hydrogenic bases whose angular content is fixed by Gaunt selection rules. This synthesis assembles the framework's quantum-computing arc—the four Group 4 papers—into a single resource-oriented narrative. The spine is: the qubit encoding and its Pauli/$1$-norm scaling [ref]; the benchmarked resource library across three periodic-table rows [ref]; the $S_N$ representation-theoretic foundation that classifies the atomic building blocks [ref]; and the nuclear shell-model extension that delineates exactly which part of the framework transfers [ref]. The unifying value proposition is structural, not accuracy-based: after the Jordan–Wigner transformation the GeoVac lattice Hamiltonian yields $\sim Q^{3.8}$ Pauli terms for atoms (corrected 2026-08-29; the retired pair-diagonal encoding gave $O(Q^{3.15})$) and a Pauli count exactly linear in qubit count for composed multi-center molecules at fixed basis (within-molecule basis exponent $3.17$; corrected 2026-08-29 from the retired $O(Q^{2.5})$) (versus $O(Q^{3.9–4.3})$ for Gaussian baselines, at whose lower edge, not below it, the atomic exponent sits), with a sub-quadratic Pauli $1$-norm $\lambda = O(Q^{1.78})$ ($R^2=0.9997$; re-measured 2026-08-30, retired: $O(Q^{1.69})$) that controls Trotter depth and qubitization query cost. Two disciplines run through the arc. First, we separate what survived the 2026-08-29 selection-rule correction from what did not. Surviving: the exact linearity $N_{\mathrm{Pauli}} = c Q$ across molecules at fixed basis, the isostructural invariance, the $Z$-independence, and the equal-qubit 1-norm advantage ($4.0×$ at $Q=10$, $7.3×$ at $Q=28$) — each re-measured under the exact rule and re-confirmed, not inherited. (The atomic figures were re-measured once more when the shipped He Hamiltonian was found to carry a non-physical $+1/16$ graph-hop one-body term; with helium's physical, diagonal one-body operator the ratios read $4.0×$ and $7.3×$ rather than $3.8×$ and $7.1×$, and the fixed-exponent GeoVac basis gives a He energy $55$–$58$ mHa above cc-pVDZ/cc-pVTZ at the same qubit count, so these atomic ratios are matched-qubit, not matched-accuracy.) Not surviving: the within-molecule and atomic exponents (which moved $2.5 \to 3.17$ and $3.15 \to 3.8$), the QWC exponent (which moved $3.36 \to 4.05$, above the term exponent, withdrawing the measurement-group advantage entirely), and every absolute multiplier. The earlier framing of this discipline — ``scaling exponents unchanged, only multipliers re-price'' — was itself retracted with the correction: the re-pricing is not a constant factor, it grows along the basis axis. Second, no comparison is at matched accuracy, and only the equal-qubit ones are at matched qubit count (the STO-3G and cc-pVDZ market tests use $Q=30$ against $12$ and $36$ for LiH): the composed basis carries classical equilibrium-geometry errors of $5.3$–$19.4%$, so the framework is positioned for fixed-geometry NISQ/VQE simulation (Pauli count, QWC measurement groups), not for fault-tolerant geometry optimisation. The nuclear extension is honest in the same way: its binding energies are encoding-validation benchmarks far from experiment, and the Fock projection rigidity theorem states precisely that the conformal $S^3$ structure does not transfer to the harmonic-oscillator basis—only the angular machinery and the qubit encoding do.

title: Gauge Structure, QED, and Gravity from the Spectral Geometry of S^3: A Synthesis of the GeoVac QED/Gauge Arc
abstract: The Geometric Vacuum (GeoVac) framework labels the hydrogen bound states by the harmonics of the unit three-sphere $S^3$ via Fock's conformal projection. This synthesis assembles the five Group 5 papers—gauge structure, the vector-photon vertex and the periods of Dirac spectral sums on $S^3$, the fine-structure-constant observation, and a spectral-action gravity sketch—into one narrative around a single organizing distinction: \emph{$U(1)$ and $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Wilson structures can be built on the graph, the choice of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ being natural because $S^3 = \mathrm{SU}(2)$, while the couplings are calibration/observation, not derived}. On the scalar label graph the plaquettes (the 4-cycles) form a cycle basis, so $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Wilson theory and its maximal-torus restriction, compact $U(1)$, are the exactly solvable two-dimensional theories, whose area law holds by factorization and carries no confinement information; on the cross-$\ell$ Dirac Rule-B graph compact $U(1)$ does not factorize and is compatible with compact electrodynamics under seven standard diagnostics, none of which discriminates a dimension [ref]; the natural gauge reach is $U(1)×\mathrm{SU}(2)×\mathrm{SU}(3)$ (an organizing reading, not a derivation), with $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ entering only as a pure-gauge theory whose natural matter coupling is obstructed. Of eight QED selection rules the scalar graph keeps one (triangle sparsity); the physical vector-photon vertex, computed exactly from $\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ representation theory, keeps triangle sparsity and $\Delta m$, satisfies the Ward–Takahashi identity, couples the ground state, and does not preserve the $1{+}6{+}1$ partition of the vertex model [ref]; the continuum $S^3$ Dirac spectral sums carry odd zeta values ($ζ(3)$, $ζ(5)$), the level-4 values Catalan $G$ and $\beta(4)$ when the spectrum is restricted to one parity class, and, in the vertex model's three-loop chain sum, the depth-2 period $ζ(5,3)$, through a depth-filtered period tower [ref]. \gvc{k-combination-rule}{The fine-structure constant approximately satisfies (to $8.8×10^{-8}$ relative; an Observation) the cubic $α^3-Kα+1=0$ with $K=π(B+F-\Delta)$ assembled from three spectral data of the unit $S^3$, each with an independently established spectral home; this is recorded strictly as an Observation (agreement $8.8×10^{-8}$, twelve single-mechanism derivations eliminated), never as a derivation [ref]}; in a look-elsewhere search of the same kind the expected chance count at this precision is about ten. The gravity paper gives a convergence theorem for a discrete replica derivative on the spinor cone (one standard ingredient argued rather than proved), and records the two-term spectral action of the round sphere (Chamseddine–Connes; an alternative proof there) and a Newton constant obtained by two routes, whose agreement (at leading order in $\Lambda$ on the black-hole cigar) is the induced-gravity statement of Susskind–Uglum and Frolov–Fursaev [ref]. The discipline throughout matches the rest of the corpus: every load-bearing claim wears its tier, the structural results are foregrounded, and the couplings are positioned as the free, calibration side of the construction.

title: Observables as Projections of a π-free Graph: A Synthesis of the GeoVac Precision-Observation Arc
abstract: The Geometric Vacuum (GeoVac) framework separates into two structurally distinct layers, and that separation is the organizing principle of its precision-observation arc. Layer 1 is a bare combinatorial graph: quantum-number labels $(n,\ell,m,\ldots)$, rational matrix entries, algebraic eigenvalues, no physical units, and—verified symbolically—no $π$. Layer 2 is a finite family of named projections from that graph onto continuous physical settings; every physical variable, every dimension, and every transcendental constant that appears in any GeoVac calculation enters through exactly one projection and is traceable to it, apart from external inputs (literature values and applied field strengths) and textbook-assembly rows that enter through no GeoVac projection. This synthesis assembles the five Group 6 papers into a single narrative built on that thesis. The spine is: the projection taxonomy and its three-axis tagging (Paper 34 [ref]); time as the prototype free-side projection—$π$ enters the Klein–Gordon spectrum on $S^3×ℝ$ at exactly one step, temporal compactification, while rest mass preserves the algebraic ring (Paper 35 [ref]); entropy as an embedding-class projection artifact, identically zero on the one-body graph and finite only after the metric embedding of the two-body repulsion (Paper 27 [ref]); and the entanglement structure that isolates that repulsion in the angular-momentum eigenbasis (Paper 26 [ref]). Roothaan autopsies close the arc:\ they decompose precision atomic observables into projection-chain-tagged components and locate framework kernel gaps; the hydrogen Lamb shift, whose leading one-loop assembly is textbook QED with tabulated Bethe logarithms (Paper 36 [ref]), is the limiting case. The literature itemization differences the autopsies meet are stated in their sources. Two disciplines run throughout. First, every transcendental named here is tagged to its projection—$π$ via the M1 volume slot (unit-sphere and Fock volumes), $π^{2k}$ via the spectral action, $ζ(2k)$ via even-zeta Dirichlet series, odd $ζ$ via the half-integer-Hurwitz spinor lift, Catalan $G$ via quarter-integer vertex parity, $2π$ via temporal compactification. Second, the precision comparisons set framework-native values against measurement, some with residuals the autopsies leave unexplained; they are not first-principles predictions of the constants, and the multi-focal-composition wall—the framework has no native theorem for composing multiple Fock-style projections—is named as an active boundary. The unifying reading is that compactness forces discreteness (the converse is false: discrete spectrum is the compact-resolvent property), made operational: the discrete skeleton is the compact/closed regime, and a transcendental is precisely the price of releasing compactness by integrating over a promoted continuous parameter.
